_note: Cross-site tuning. These are opinions, not measurements -- kept here so a step never has to be edited to change one, and so the assumptions a model was built under are visible in one file.

widths_m._note: carriageway width, pavement each side. Draw order and any rendering lift belong to the consumer, not to this data.

roads.chaikin_note: Corner-cutting to stop OSM's angular vertices reading as facets. It MOVES the centreline, by up to a quarter of the vertex spacing -- a presentation choice, not a survey. Set to 0 for geometry faithful to OSM; the value used is recorded in the manifest.

rail.classes_note: OSM railway values emitted by step 11 as cls. disused = track still in place; abandoned/razed/dismantled have no track and are skipped, as are platform/station/signal and other non-track ways. Skipped values are counted in linear_manifest.ways_skipped_by_class.
rail.default_gauge_note: Standard gauge (1435 mm), the whole Kent network. OSM gauge is in millimetres and is converted; a way without the tag gets this and gauge_src=default.
rail.chaikin_note: Same presentation choice as roads. The Streetscape rail profile resamples with curvature-adaptive spacing anyway. Set 0 for OSM-faithful vertices.

barriers.classes_note: OSM barrier values emitted by step 11 as cls -- the linear ones. gate and bollard ways (two-node, point-like) and barrier=yes are skipped and counted; barrier nodes live in the points layer.
barriers.default_height_note: OPINIONS, used only when OSM has no height tag (Margate: 15 of 467 barrier ways carry one) and tagged h_src=default. wall 1.8 (below the 2 m permitted-development limit); fence 1.5 (garden panel); hedge 1.5 (trimmed privet); retaining_wall 1.5 (the DTM step is the truth); kerb 0.12 (= furniture.kerb_m); guard_rail 0.75 (beam height); handrail 1.0 (Approved Document K); city_wall 6.0 (placeholder).
barriers.chaikin_note: Zero on purpose: walls and fences are angular; Chaikin would move every corner a quarter-span inward. Densification still adds drape points every 8 m.

buildings.min_pixels_note: Fewer LIDAR samples than this inside a footprint and p50 is noise; the height is still emitted but tagged lidar_lowconf.
buildings.percentile_note: p50 as the wall/body height and p90 as the ridge: p99 and max chase chimneys and aerials, the mean is dragged down by roof pitch.
buildings.skirt_note: How far below the lowest sampled ground a footprint's skirt extends, so a building on a slope does not float at its downhill edge.
buildings.flat_roof_note: static_caravan added after the Whitby extract showed 359 of them (caravan parks): low, near-flat roofs, and a gabled default read wrong at walking distance.

type_priors_m._note: LAST-RESORT heights for footprints with no OSM height, no levels and no usable LIDAR. Measured from Margate's own LIDAR, so they encode one town's vernacular -- a different settlement pattern wants its own set. Records that fall back to these are tagged src=type_prior and counted in the run summary; if that count is large for a new site, re-measure rather than shipping Margate's terraces.

coast.class_res_note: Ground-classification raster resolution per tile edge. Must divide the tile size in pixels exactly; step 09 fails loudly if it does not.

furniture.props_note: OSM amenity value -> an abstract prop key. Mapping a key to a mesh is the consumer's job.
furniture.snap_note: Further than this from any road centreline, the road tells us nothing about elevation; leave it null and let the consumer drape onto terrain.
furniture.kerb_note: How far a pavement top sits above the carriageway centreline. A property of how the consumer builds roads -- override per project.
